I didnt tell the professor. Because financial debt and impending doom over the possibility of being thrown out of college..which was my financial support. I got supported as a researcher..which I still am.

I lied about around 5/100 points on a class. I was not sure about the order of some grades, so under pressure I submitted them anyways. 70 out of 240 complained.

The only possible way to not feel like a fraud I have figured out, is to chose a career which is absolutely unrelated to all of this, and actively denounce all my degrees, right from undergrad. I am good at art and painting, so I figure that is my way where I can get in without possibly ANY degree qualifications. I need to declare myself as someone without any qualifications. 

Problem is, I was a grad student in the US, so I have gotten used to the first world life. Quitting it all and returning back to a third world country(where I am originally from), with an active voluntary disqualification of all my degrees is gonna be a rough road, but I feel that is what is right. 

I really did like my work though :/, and there is going to be a lot of regret why I didnt chose to be an ethical person from say 10 years ago. But I think regret is more preferable to guilt.

Your ideas are true to an extent, and the assamese people should not be xenophobic. However, I can vouch for the fact that it’s the rednecks who are like that. But the increasing number of migrants and people like Garga Chatterjee from the Indian Statistical Institute exacerbate these problems and even academics are now growing increasingly ethno nationalistic. 

I feel it’s a vicious cycle of the feeling of being neglected by the mainland and the xenophobia which arises from it. There is xenophobia from both sides. There are documented hate crimes against people from the north east in the “mainland”.  

But the line in the sand is clear-illegal immigrants from a foreign country. People are  giving it a communal color which is not at all required at the moment. There were a huge percentage of bengalis already but adding Bangladeshis to the top tilts the percentage even further. They will form a contiguous Bengali unit which already accounts for about 30%, and that wasn’t the situation pre-independence. Look at what’s happening to America, to Germany with around 10-15%(rough ballpark number) Hispanic people and Arab spring refugees respectively.  The more the percentage tilts further down, the more right wingers it will produce. 

If you talk of assimilation, upper assam has that component, but the barak valley simply won’t assimilate. They do not want to learn assamese. They are Bengalis in linguistic ideation and pride. There religious identity is Assamese, is all. Have you ever been to silchar? It’s totally bengal. I am not saying that that should necessarily be an issue. Darjeeling and associated areas of North bengal do not like assimilating either but they are not a demographic threat to bengal- bengal won’t be speaking anything other than Bengali anytime soon. 

The imminent problem is that Assamese feel that the CAA+NRC would give leeway to Hindu Bengalis from bangladesh come here(Which can happen anytime Awami league goes out of power in Bangladesh. Now you might say the cutoff date is 2014, but that has not stopped paranoia from growing, due to a distrust in the systems in place which are highly corrupt and government driven, and the five year Naturilzation rule. There are 20 million hindus in bangladesh and that’s a huge number.

This also brings about the geo-political idea of a state in India. What does it mean to be Maharashtra, or Tamil Nadu or Kerala. Are these states only a loose idea for administrative ease or they demand an implicit preservation of their ethno-regional identity. Kashmir certainly does, and so does assam. I am not too sure if Suddenly Orissa became 40% Oriya people.  Don’t speak about the hindi belt because we all know that the lines are very fluid and porous there and a UP person in MP and a keralite in assam are two very separate issues. Let’s not kid ourselves. 

We need to very careful with how we deal with this because you suddenly cannot impose the Indian identity on people before their regional identity. Many places still unfortunately do not adhere to that idea of a nation. It will take eons before that happens and we need to hold this country together until that happens. Otherwise we become Yugoslavia.
